text:
Priya (Infra): Quick follow-up from the CP-handshake RFC — I sketched a small reorg to reduce cross-account NAT blast radius and make handoff semantics explicit. Wanted feedback before I open a PR.

Dan K: Sketch it here pls — short notes fine.

Priya (Infra): TL;DR: split responsibilities so CP only performs authn/authz + route selection. Tenant-side 'egress operator' owns SNAT, public IP allocation, and health-probing. That way we can scale CP without carrying per-tenant IP state.

Miguel O: Nice. How do we handle fallback when operator is misbehaving (eg operator crashes, IPs leaked)?

Priya (Infra): Good Q. Proposal: add a transient fallback mode on CP that will NAT for in-flight sessions only, with telemetry + rate-limited leak cleanup. Full takeover requires an explicit admin switch and TTL-based IP rebind.

Zoe L: Can we avoid introducing a new long-lived API surface? I'd prefer extending current connector handshake rather than a separate operator CRD if possible.

Priya (Infra): I considered both. Connector handshake extension gets messy because connector pods live in tenant VPCs and we'd still need a cluster-side controller to manage global IPs + billing. The 'egress operator' is a small controller that runs in tenant account (or customer-managed) and talks to CP via a tightly-scoped ephemeral token.

Raj P: Ephemeral token flow sounds fine. Needs rotation + audit events. Does this change cert flow?

Priya (Infra): Minimal change: keep mutual TLS for control-plane channel. Add an operator token for lease ops with a short TTL; rotation handled by existing cert-rotator. Audit logs: CP will emit operator-lease events with tenant_id and lease_id.

Miguel O: Would love a proto sketch of the lease API.

Priya (Infra): Posted a tiny diff idea:

```proto
// egress.proto
message EgressLeaseRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string operator_id = 2;
  uint32 num_ips = 3;
  string ttl = 4; // ISO8601
}
message EgressLeaseResponse {
  string lease_id = 1;
  repeated string public_ips = 2;
  string expires_at = 3;
}
service EgressManager {
  rpc AcquireLease(EgressLeaseRequest) returns (EgressLeaseResponse);
  rpc ReleaseLease(LeaseId) returns (Empty);
}
```

Dan K: Looks straightforward. How about migration path? We have 3k tenants on legacy flow.

Priya (Infra): Migration plan (draft):
- Phase 0: opt-in only, operator runs in tenant account (beta)
- Phase 1: dual-mode for new tenants; CP can NAT for non-operator tenants but emits warnings
- Phase 2: require operator for new Dedicated and Private customers; provide a managed operator for enterprise customers
- Phase 3: deprecate CP full-NAT path after 3 months of adoption

Zoe L: Can we add a runtime flag to disable CP-NAT early for test tenants? I'd like to validate failure modes.

Priya (Infra): Yep — runtime feature-flag gated + rollout via console. We'll also add a canary group to observe error spikes and token churn.

Miguel O: Ops concerns: IP churn will affect customers using IP-based allowlists. Need communication and sticky-lease option.

Priya (Infra): We'll include a sticky_lease boolean and a migration doc for allowlist customers — recommend updating allowlists to CIDR ranges where possible.

Raj P: Security: ensure operator can't arbitrarily request leases for other tenants. Enforce tenant_id in token claims and CP-side validation.

Priya (Infra): Agreed — token claims + MTLS + lease ACLs. Also adding audit hooks to the console.

ops-bot: Deployed prototype handler to staging: https://staging.redwood.internal/egress-lease (beta).

Dan K: Nice. Action items?

Priya (Infra): Short list: 
- I will open RFC addendum PR with proto + state machine (this week).
- @Dan K to validate fallback NAT behavior and cleanup in the simulator (next sprint).
- @Miguel O to draft migration comms for IP allowlist customers.
- @Zoe L to evaluate connector-handshake delta and confirm if we can avoid adding new CRDs.

Dan K: Ack, will add sim tests.

Miguel O: Will draft comms.

Zoe L: I'll run a connector spike and post results.

Priya (Infra): Thanks all. If nobody objects I'll open the PR tomorrow and tag infra/security for review. :thumbsup:
